questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code handles transactions and concurrent stock allocation? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Two workers call allocate_shipment with the same shipment_id at the same moment, and the first one commits successfully. What does the second worker end up returning?
choices: It raises IntegrityError, and run_in_transaction retries the whole call from scratch.
It allocates a second, independent set of bins, because READ COMMITTED lets both transactions see free stock.
Its INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING waits for the first transaction, inserts nothing, and it returns the picks the first worker recorded without touching stock.
It returns an empty list immediately because the claim failed and nothing was allocated.

questions.prompt: Both allocate_shipment and move_between_bins lock rows with order_by(StockBin.id) (or sorted ids) before FOR UPDATE. What does that ordering buy?
choices: Every transaction acquires row locks in the same global order, so two overlapping transactions cannot each hold a lock the other is waiting for.
It lets PostgreSQL use the index on sku, which FOR UPDATE requires.
It guarantees the oldest stock is picked first, which is what the business rule requires for correctness of the reservation counts.
It prevents lost updates on the reserved column, which would otherwise happen even while the rows are locked.

questions.prompt: allocate_shipment has claimed the shipment, incremented reserved on two bins, and then raises InsufficientStock because the third bin was not enough. What state does the database end up in?
choices: The reserved increments stay, so the partial stock is held for a later attempt.
Only the allocation_requests row stays, so a later call with the same shipment_id returns an empty list.
Only the Allocation rows stay, because they were added after the claim.
Nothing changes: the exception leaves the session.begin() block, which rolls back the claim row, the reservations and the allocations together, and the exception is not retried.
